channel.title: Heather Lyn Wilson
channel.description: Faith, leadership, and what stood out from my Bible reading. New posts Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

item.title: While He Was Still Speaking
item.description: One messenger has not even finished before another shows up with worse news. And then another. The first thing Job did was fall on his face in worship.

item.title: Job's Regular Practice
item.description: Long before Job lost everything, he was just a dad who got up early to intercede for his kids. Not panic prayer. A rhythm.

item.title: Mercy Received
item.description: The Jews had just been rescued by God. And then the way they handled their new power scared everyone around them. Mercy received did not always become mercy given.

item.title: Maybe I Have Had a Hard-Fought Hallelujah
item.description: Standing in church singing about a hard-fought hallelujah, I realized I actually have had a few. I just don't reach for them first when I think about my life.

item.title: Why I Highlighted This One
item.description: There is a part of me that reads this verse and thinks good. That is the honest answer. And I am not sure what to do with that.

item.title: The Verse Without the Coffee Mug
item.description: Esther was not picking out a coffee mug. She was about to walk in to a king's throne room uninvited, knowing the law said she could be killed for it.

item.title: They Read It and Went and Did It
item.description: They studied the Word, saw something they had been missing, and went and did it. No committee. No five-year plan. They just went.

item.title: When Fear Wears a Friendly Face
item.description: It is one thing when the bad guys are clearly the bad guys. It is harder when someone you trusted leans on your fear to push you out of obedience.

item.title: 5 Signs You're Consuming Christian Content Instead of Actually Growing
item.description: A lot of us are consuming more than we ever have and growing less than we ever have. And the scary part is we do not always know the difference.

item.title: Remember Me
item.description: We all want to be seen. We all want our quiet faithfulness to count for something. Nehemiah just asked it of the only One who actually sees.

item.title: The Gracious Hand of God
item.description: Nehemiah could have walked out of that throne room patting himself on the back. Instead he walked out with his eyes on the One who had been moving in the background.

item.title: Pray Before You Speak
item.description: Before he was the man who rebuilt a city, Nehemiah was a cupbearer who knew how to pause and pray in the middle of a sentence.

item.title: Highlighted: 2 Chronicles 31:1
item.description: They did not just go home and get back to their normal life. They left the festival and went to every town they could reach, and they tore down idols.

item.title: Highlighted: 2 Chronicles 28:23
item.description: He looked at the army that just destroyed him and thought their gods must be working. So he sacrificed to the gods of his enemies. And it led to his ruin.

item.title: Careful
item.description: Jotham was the son of a king who fell in pride. He took the good of his father's life and left the bad. We can too.

item.title: What Rises in Pride
item.description: What we see playing out in our culture today is not new. King Uzziah was the same story. Power. Pride. A line crossed. A public collapse.

item.title: The Gospel Hiding in the Law
item.description: Tucked into a chapter about a king and his enemies is one of the clearest pictures of the gospel I have ever seen.

item.title: 2 Chronicles 22:12
item.description: Athaliah ruled for six years thinking she had wiped out the royal line. She had not. There was a boy in the temple. And he was the rightful king.

item.title: 2 Chronicles 20:15
item.description: We default to fighting. Strategizing. Hustling. But sometimes God says sit down, watch, and let Me handle this one. Those might be the hardest seasons to obey.

item.title: He Did Not Even Pray
item.description: Same Asa who once cried out to God against an army of a million. Now he is sick and does not even pray. The progression is sobering.
